query: Write me a systemd service and timer pair that runs /usr/local/bin/nightly-backup every night at 2:00 local time, and say where each file goes.
result:
Both files go in `/etc/systemd/system/`, the system unit directory. On this machine (pavilion, Bluefin DX), keep the source copies in `~/.dotfiles/bluefin/etc/systemd/system/` and link them into `/etc` from there, so the dotfiles copy stays the record.

**`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.service`**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Nightly backup

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nightly-backup
```

**`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.timer`**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run nightly-backup every night at 02:00 local time

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

`OnCalendar` uses the system's local time zone, so 02:00 means 2:00 on the wall clock. `Persistent=true` makes systemd run a missed job at the next boot if the desktop was off at 2:00. Without it, a powered-down machine skips that night's backup.

The service has no `[Install]` section because the timer starts it. The timer's `Unit=` defaults to the service with the same name, so I left it out.

The service runs as root because no user was given. If the script should run as your user, add `User=glw907` under `[Service]`, and check that the script can write its destination as that user.

To turn it on, run `sudo systemctl daemon-reload` and then `sudo systemctl enable --now nightly-backup.timer`. Then `systemctl list-timers nightly-backup.timer` shows the next run time. I have not created or enabled these units. If you want me to write them into the dotfiles tree, link them, and enable the timer, say so.
